scenario: A default email deadline and an explained WeChat override are confirmed from one governed source under v1. A rolled-back future v2 transition must affect only new confirmation, preserve all v1 semantics, and prevent published policy mutation, deletion, or overlap.
frozen_evidence: 14 backend test files and 100 tests passing

review_plan.reason: Policy defaults and overrides can create or prevent recurring recruiter maintenance work.
The slice controls temporal identity authority, published policy immutability, override provenance, and privacy-safe history.
The frozen slice proves backend and Agent-history semantics; exact Web and iOS override interaction remains a named next test.
Freshness policy governs identity evidence review and does not assess, score, rank, or predict a person.
The artifact is internal governance and performs no candidate-facing communication or external action.

reviews.lens: boutique recruiter control, explanation burden, and maintenance value

findings.observation: The system now preserves exactly which rule produced a review deadline and never silently moves old deadlines when a future policy is introduced. The 180, 365, and 730-day intervals remain unvalidated product assumptions.
findings.evidence: The runtime records v1 on default and overridden clues, proves a synthetic 30-day v2 affects only a new confirmation, and preserves both v1 deadlines; no recruiter field distribution is frozen.
findings.user_impact: The recruiter can trust the history, but a poor interval could still create premature maintenance work for long-lived executive relationships or leave recycled identifiers current too long.
findings.recommendation: Calibrate by handle type and issuer using correction, expiry, reconfirmation, dismissal, and task-blocking observations; change defaults only through a new named policy.
findings.verification: Across consented or synthetic recruiter portfolios, report review volume, useful-review rate, wrong-current-handle rate, correction latency, dismissal rate, and time saved for each policy cohort.

findings.observation: A custom deadline requires a meaningful recruiter reason and the reason is visible later in Agent history. The exact entry, preview, and correction interaction is not yet proven on Web or iOS.
findings.evidence: The backend rejects an unexplained custom deadline and persists a valid reason; the runtime inspects durable Agent history, not a browser or device flow.
findings.user_impact: A rare expert override is safer, but exposing policy vocabulary or a free-form form in ordinary capture could turn a fast contact save into configuration work.
findings.recommendation: Keep the policy default implicit in normal intake. Reveal a custom deadline only behind a concise Change review date action, show the consequence, and allow later correction from history.
findings.verification: Recruiters complete ordinary saves without seeing policy controls, while expert users can set, explain, review, and correct an override in under one minute with no raw-handle exposure.

strengths: The recruiter no longer has to remember why a contact clue expires on a particular date; the policy or explicit override travels with the decision.
Future product tuning cannot silently rewrite older relationship history or extend identity authority.
An expert can choose a shorter or longer bounded review interval when issuer behavior is known, but must leave an understandable reason.
Agent history turns policy metadata into plain operational memory instead of exposing a database field.
Ordinary intake still uses a default and does not require the recruiter to configure every phone, email, or WeChat clue.
No candidate-facing communication or external system mutation occurs in the policy workflow.
missing_evidence: Measured review usefulness and burden for the v1 intervals across working recruiters.
Exact Web and iOS override entry, preview, correction, and accessibility proof.
At-scale Today prioritization that prevents policy deadlines from becoming generic CRM cleanup.
Issuer-specific evidence for shared, recycled, employer-controlled, and source-native identifiers.
open_questions: Should normal recruiters ever see the policy version, or only a plain-language reason and review date?
Should longer-than-default extensions require a second confirmation or stronger source than shorter safety-oriented intervals?

reviews.lens: temporal identity governance, policy immutability, human override authority, and privacy
strengths: Every new identity confirmation resolves one effective policy at confirmation time and snapshots its version, final deadline, validity basis, and optional human override reason on the handle.
The same policy snapshot is copied into immutable lifecycle history and privacy-safe audit metadata rather than inferred later from current configuration.
Default intervals live in a versioned policy document, while a custom deadline fails closed unless the recruiter supplies a bounded visible reason.
A reason without a custom deadline also fails closed, preventing meaningless or misleading override metadata.
The policy maximum bounds both defaults and human overrides; an invalid or unavailable policy stops confirmation instead of falling back silently.
Published policy content, version, effective start, and maximum cannot be edited or deleted. The database permits only one-way retirement followed by a non-overlapping successor.
A rolled-back v2 transition directly proves that new confirmations can use v2 while existing v1 policy versions and exact deadlines remain unchanged.
The human override basis and reason appear in durable relationship Agent history so the decision remains understandable after reload.
Raw email, WeChat, and phone values remain absent from the identity index, lifecycle projection, audit projection, and Agent history.
The slice performs no automatic person decision or consequential external write.
missing_evidence: Field calibration of each default interval using observed corrections, reconfirmations, and issuer-specific identifier behavior.
A privileged production deployment proof showing that only migration governance can retire or add policies.
Concurrent policy retirement and confirmation tests at the exact effective-time boundary.
Exact Web and iOS review copy for a human override, including accessibility and later explanation.
open_questions: Should source-native identifiers name an issuer-specific policy instead of sharing one generic 180-day interval?
Which roles, if any, may set a custom identity deadline, and should an extension require stronger evidence than a shorter interval?

top_findings.reason: Versioning makes later learning safe, but v1's 180, 365, and 730-day defaults are not yet supported by recruiter field observations.
top_findings.next_step: Measure review usefulness and identity correction outcomes by handle type and issuer before proposing v2.
top_findings.verification: A policy cohort report shows useful-review, wrong-current-handle, correction, dismissal, time-saved, and review-burden rates without ranking people.

top_findings.reason: The authoritative backend and durable history are proven, while the exact optional override control has not been tested on Web or iOS.
top_findings.next_step: Keep normal saves default-only and test a progressive Change review date interaction with preview and correction.
top_findings.verification: Ordinary capture gains no configuration step; an expert override remains understandable, reversible, accessible, and under one minute.

agreements: Both selected reviewers agree that every identity deadline must retain its policy version and final timestamp rather than be recomputed from current defaults.
Both selected reviewers agree that future policy changes must affect only new confirmation and never silently extend prior authority.
Both selected reviewers agree that a custom deadline requires a visible human reason and should remain exceptional.
Both selected reviewers agree that published policy content must be immutable and policy intervals non-overlapping.
Both selected reviewers agree that current v1 intervals still require field calibration before production claims.
adjudication.rationale: The technical policy boundary passes: runtime evidence proves effective-time policy selection, durable version and basis snapshots, explained overrides, visible Agent history, a future v2 transition that leaves v1 unchanged, published-policy immutability, overlap prevention, privacy-safe projections, and zero external writes. The broader release remains needs-evidence because v1 interval calibration and exact optional Web/iOS interaction have not been proven with working recruiters.

next_tests.test: Policy cohort calibration with recruiter portfolios
next_tests.evidence_required: Consented or synthetic portfolio observations by handle type and issuer, including useful reviews, wrong-current clues, corrections, dismissals, task blocks, time saved, and review burden.
next_tests.pass_condition: A proposed v2 interval has observed benefit and no unacceptable review fatigue, privacy concern, or identity error increase.

next_tests.pass_condition: Normal capture has no added configuration burden and an expert override is understandable, reversible, and under one minute.

next_tests.evidence_required: Concurrent confirmations immediately before, at, and after a policy boundary plus simultaneous attempted policy retirement or overlap.
next_tests.pass_condition: Every confirmation resolves exactly one immutable policy, no interval overlaps, and prior records remain unchanged.

next_tests.evidence_required: Simulator or device proof with VoiceOver, Dynamic Type, keyboard, interruption, offline retry, duplicate submission, and return to Agent history.
next_tests.pass_condition: The optional override and its later explanation remain legible, recoverable, and single-effect without exposing raw identity values.
